summary: Three-way fidelity audit: does the HTML doc match what the code actually does, and do both still serve THE IDEA of spec-loop?
logs: Extracting concrete, checkable claims from deck + playbook + one-pager, then verifying each against the real code.
171 doc claims checked · 41 disagree with code · 7 external/unverifiable. Idea-drift from 2 lenses.

reconciliation.fidelity_verdict: The doc does NOT faithfully represent the code — it is a marketing-grade narrative that repeatedly promises mechanization the 2153-line engine does not have. The code itself is honest and internally consistent (its own comments disclaim what it doesn't do: 'NOT AST cyclomatic complexity', 'abstraction INTENTIONALLY not weighted', 'eso es proceso, no código', converged/readiness labeled ADVISORY). The betrayal runs one direction: the deck/playbook/onepager fabricate features (a /qa command, profiles A-E, a 7-layer bootstrap, a size-warning hook, scoop/gentle-ai install steps, a 520/17,022 security stat, a spec-loop-claude-code-doc-EN.html) and overstate real ones ('CONSTITUTION breach blocks convergence by construction', 'readiness BLOCKS', 'simplicity normalized to the static severity scale'). The single most damaging drift is that the orchestrator SKILL.md — the doc a reader actually runs — never mentions golden capture, .approved/.received, or the PreToolUse hook, so the tenet the marketing leans on hardest (tenet 5, 'the artifact the agent cannot author') is unreachable on the main path despite being fully backed in code and CONSTITUTION. Net: the CODE serves the idea better than the DOC does; the fix is overwhelmingly to soften/correct the doc down to what the engine actually enforces, plus a few small code wires (version field, and optionally making golden/gate load-bearing in convergence).
reconciliation.accuracy_score: Of ~30 load-bearing doc claims I re-verified against qa_ledger.py, the SKILL.md files, and the kit tree, ~10 were ACCURATE-as-stated and ~20 were wrong or materially overstated → roughly 33% accurate (10/30). The upstream findings package itself was ~97% accurate (29/30 findings held on re-check); the one correction: the playbook '// ADR: <slug>' claim was ruled FALSE for 'no marker exists in the kit', but the marker IS documented at dev-loop/SKILL.md:97 — so that doc claim is largely SUPPORTED and its finding is downgraded to 'no gate enforces the marker'.

discrepancies.claim: A CONSTITUTION violation is logged as a BLOCKER finding, caps readiness at ≤65, and blocks convergence
discrepancies.doc_quote: A violation is logged as a BLOCKER finding → caps readiness ≤65 and blocks convergence by construction.
discrepancies.code_does: The readiness ≤65 cap ('blocker_critical', DEFAULT_CAPS line 796) fires only from `sev.get("BLOCKER",0)+sev.get("CRITICAL",0)` (qa_ledger.py:888-890), and that `sev` dict is built exclusively from static-gate `severity_counts` via `_gate_open_and_sev`/`_latest_static_by_tool` (835-843, 624-629). Those severity counts are produced ONLY by `cmd_ingest_gate` parsing Checkstyle/PMD/SpotBugs/FindSecBugs XML (534-611, sev_counts at 593-595, category 'static-gate' at 600). Agent findings logged via `cmd_log_step` carry NO severity field at all (506-522). Convergence (`_converged`, 632-655; `cmd_converged`, 658-672) never inspects severity — it only checks agent gated_reported, files_changed, green tests, and static-gate gated counts. There is no code path anywhere in qa_ledger.py that recognizes a 'CONSTITUTION violation' as a concept or maps it to a BLOCKER severity count. So a CONSTITUTION invariant (e.g. an architectural/security rule) has no automated route to the BLOCKER cap unless it happens to coincide with a linter rule whose severity resolves to BLOCKER (SEVERITY_ORDER line 277, PMD_PRIORITY line 282).
discrepancies.delta: The doc's phrase 'by construction' claims a structural/automatic guarantee. The engine has no CONSTITUTION-awareness: the ≤65 cap and convergence block ONLY react to linter-derived severity/gated counts from ingest-gate. A CONSTITUTION violation becomes a BLOCKER only if a human/agent manually logs it as such — and log-step (the agent path) has no severity field, so it cannot even record a BLOCKER. Thus 'logged as a BLOCKER finding -> caps readiness -> blocks convergence by construction' is true only when the violation coincidentally maps to a BLOCKER-tier linter finding; for the typical CONSTITUTION invariant it is a manual convention, not a construction-level guarantee. Also, convergence blocks on gated counts, not on 'BLOCKER' severity per se.
discrepancies.fix: Reword to reflect that the enforcement is a convention, not automatic. E.g.: 'By project convention, a CONSTITUTION violation MUST be recorded as a BLOCKER-severity finding. When it is (via a linter rule at BLOCKER tier ingested through `ingest-gate`), the readiness cap of 65 fires and the gated finding blocks convergence. The dev-loop engine does not detect CONSTITUTION breaches itself — the agent must stop and escalate; the ≤65 cap only reacts to BLOCKER/CRITICAL severity counts from static-gate reports.' Remove 'by construction'.

discrepancies.claim: simplicity-check is a qa_ledger.py subcommand that scores and stops deterministically, normalized to the same severity scale as the static gate
discrepancies.doc_quote: A qa_ledger.py simplicity-check subcommand that scores and stops — deterministic, zero opinion. ... Normalized to the same severity scale as the static gate.
discrepancies.code_does: simplicity-check is a real qa_ledger.py subcommand (cmd_simplicity_check, qa_ledger.py:1466) that DOES score and stop deterministically: it derives metrics from diff text (_simplicity_metrics, :1333), scores with fixed weights (_simplicity_score, :1411), and exits deterministically via sys.exit(0 if verdict != "OVERBUILT" else 1) (:1490, :1514). BUT it is NOT normalized to the static gate's severity scale. The static gate scale is SEVERITY_ORDER = ["INFO","LOW","MEDIUM","HIGH","CRITICAL","BLOCKER"] (:277). simplicity-check instead produces a 0-100 score mapped to a wholly separate band set SIMPLICITY_BANDS = [(85,"SIMPLE"),(65,"ACCEPTABLE"),(0,"OVERBUILT")] (:1067, _simplicity_band :1098). Its output object (:1485-1487) emits only score/verdict(SIMPLE|ACCEPTABLE|OVERBUILT)/weights/dimensions/metrics/budgets/flags — it never emits or maps to INFO/LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL/BLOCKER, and no code path bridges the two scales.
discrepancies.delta: The claim is a conjunction; its first half (deterministic scoring + stop) holds, but the second half ("Normalized to the same severity scale as the static gate") is contradicted by the code. The static gate and simplicity-check use two independent, disjoint verdict vocabularies (INFO..BLOCKER vs SIMPLE/ACCEPTABLE/OVERBUILT) with no normalization between them. simplicity-check is scored on a 0-100 numeric scale banded into 3 simplicity-specific labels, not the 6-level severity ladder used for static-analysis findings.
discrepancies.fix: Drop the "Normalized to the same severity scale as the static gate" sentence, or correct it to state that simplicity-check has its own 0-100 score with SIMPLE/ACCEPTABLE/OVERBUILT bands (distinct from the static gate's INFO..BLOCKER severity scale). Keep the accurate first half about deterministic scoring and stopping.

discrepancies.claim: simplicity-check enforces caps on added lines, added files, added deps, and cyclomatic complexity per method

discrepancies.claim: gate-check flags a diff that deletes/skips tests, disables lint, lowers thresholds, or rewrites a mass of asserts as a BLOCKER, deterministic, exit 1
discrepancies.doc_quote: A diff that deletes or skips tests, disables lint, lowers thresholds, or rewrites a mass of asserts is a BLOCKER until human justification. It's measured by qa_ledger.py gate-check — deterministic, exit 1.
discrepancies.code_does: cmd_gate_check (qa_ledger.py:1652-1733) splits its signals into HARD and SOFT. Only removed tests (`removed_tests`, l.1690-91), disabled/skipped tests (`disabled_tests`, l.1676-77), and lowered thresholds (`thresholds`, l.1684-85) go into `hard` (l.1698) and produce verdict BLOCKER with `sys.exit(1)` deterministically (l.1700-01, 1733). Lint suppressions (`suppressions`, l.1678-79) and rewritten/removed asserts (`assertions_removed`, l.1692-93) go into `soft` (l.1699); by default they yield verdict REVIEW and `sys.exit(0)` — they only become a BLOCKER/exit 1 when `--strict` is passed (`blocker = hard > 0 or (args.strict and soft > 0)`, l.1700). The code's own comment (l.1622-25) states this exact split.
discrepancies.delta: The doc puts all four triggers ("deletes or skips tests, disables lint, lowers thresholds, or rewrites a mass of asserts") into a single BLOCKER / exit-1 category. In reality only three (delete tests, skip/disable tests, lower thresholds) are hard BLOCKERs that exit 1 by default. "Disables lint" (suppressions) and "rewrites a mass of asserts" are SOFT signals → verdict REVIEW, exit 0 by default; they only block/exit 1 under the non-default --strict flag. So 2 of the 4 listed items do not behave as the doc claims unless --strict is set.
discrepancies.fix: Split the doc sentence to match the code: "A diff that deletes/skips tests or lowers thresholds is a BLOCKER (exit 1) by default. Adding lint suppressions or removing/rewriting asserts is a soft signal (verdict REVIEW, exit 0) that only becomes a blocker under --strict. Measured deterministically by qa_ledger.py gate-check via regex over a git diff."

discrepancies.claim: Fact gates (golden-diff, pit-check, gate-check, readiness/rebuild, simplicity/caps) BLOCK; prose heuristics (spec-check, abstractions) ADVISE

discrepancies.code_does: Per-subcommand exit codes in qa_ledger.py: golden-diff `sys.exit(0 if passed else 1)` (lines 1938/1952) → blocks; pit-check `sys.exit(0 if passed else 1)` (1598/1616) → blocks; gate-check `sys.exit(1 if blocker else 0)` (1712/1733) → blocks; rebuild(compare) `sys.exit(0 if verdict=="COVERS" else 1)` (1262/1273) → blocks; simplicity-check `sys.exit(0 if verdict!="OVERBUILT" else 1)` (1490/1514) → blocks; spec-check `fail = args.strict and n_find > 0` then `sys.exit(1 if fail else 0)` (1859/1864/1881) → advisory unless --strict. BUT cmd_readiness (lines 906-1023) contains NO sys.exit call at all — it only `return`s and prints, so it ALWAYS exits 0. Confirmed by grepping every sys.exit in the file (488,490,672,689,692,1262,1273,1294,1299,1490,1514,1580,1585,1598,1616,1712,1733,1850,1855,1864,1881,1938,1942,1952) — none falls in the 906-1023 readiness range. readiness is a scoring/reporting command, not a process gate; it cannot block on its own exit code.
discrepancies.delta: The claim bundles "readiness / rebuild ... BLOCKS", asserting both block as fact-gates. rebuild does block (exit 1 unless COVERS), but readiness NEVER blocks: cmd_readiness has zero sys.exit calls and always terminates with exit 0, printing a score/band. So the claim is correct for golden-diff, pit-check, gate-check, rebuild, simplicity/caps (BLOCK) and for spec-check (ADVISES), but overstates readiness — it is really an advisory/reporting command, not a blocking gate. The convergence-capping mentioned elsewhere (SKILL.md: readiness capped ≤65 blocks convergence "by construction") is enforced by OTHER gates/logic, not by readiness's own exit code.
discrepancies.fix: Split readiness out of the BLOCKS row. State it as: "readiness ... REPORTS/ADVISES (always exit 0; it scores and caps but does not gate the process); rebuild ... BLOCKS (exit 1 unless COVERS)." Keep the other five (golden-diff, pit-check, gate-check, rebuild, simplicity/caps) as BLOCKS and spec-check/abstractions as ADVISES.

discrepancies.claim: An ADR is written only if the decision is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off (all three)
discrepancies.doc_quote: Only if the decision meets all three: hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off.
discrepancies.code_does: adr-refine/SKILL.md defines ADR-worthiness only as "One ADR per decision worth recording" (line 84), with the sole enforced requirement being that "Every decision has a rationale and at least one considered alternative" (line 68; echoed by the ADR template's "opciones consideradas"/"Razones", lines 90-94). It also explicitly says negative decisions count (line 107). Nowhere does the file state the three-part gate the doc claims.
discrepancies.delta: The doc claims a strict conjunctive three-legged test — an ADR is written ONLY IF the decision is (1) hard to reverse AND (2) surprising without context AND (3) the result of a real trade-off. The SKILL.md contains none of these three phrases. "Hard to reverse" and "surprising without context" appear nowhere at all. Only the "real trade-off" leg has a loose analogue (the required "considered alternative"), and even that is a per-recorded-decision formatting/convergence requirement, not a gate deciding WHETHER something merits an ADR. The doc thus invents a specific, restrictive worthiness filter that the skill does not implement — and it actually contradicts the skill's inclusive stance ("decision worth recording", "negative decisions count").
discrepancies.fix: Either (doc) rewrite the claim to match the skill: "An ADR is written for each decision worth recording; the only hard requirement is that it carries a rationale plus at least one considered alternative — negative decisions (what NOT to use) count too." Or (code) if the three-part gate is genuinely the intended policy, add it explicitly to adr-refine/SKILL.md Phase B as the ADR-worthiness filter, so the skill and doc agree.

discrepancies.claim: simplicity-check can be invoked with --from-git and flags OVERBUILT (example: a DiscountStrategyFactory for 3 lines)
discrepancies.doc_quote: simplicity-check --from-git → OVERBUILT: the agent added a DiscountStrategyFactory for 3 lines.
discrepancies.code_does: `simplicity-check --from-git` is a real command: the subparser registers `--from-git` (qa_ledger.py:2072) and `cmd_simplicity_check` reads the diff via `git diff --unified=0 <base>` (qa_ledger.py:1284-1294). OVERBUILT is a real verdict band, returned for scores below 65 (SIMPLICITY_BANDS at qa_ledger.py:1067; `_simplicity_band` at 1098-1102; verdict assigned at 1482). BUT the doc's illustrative example — "a DiscountStrategyFactory for 3 lines" flagged OVERBUILT — describes behavior the code intentionally does NOT implement. The `abstraction` dimension (new types/factories) is computed (qa_ledger.py:1416-1419) but is NOT in SIMPLICITY_WEIGHTS (qa_ledger.py:1064-1066), and the score only sums over those weights (qa_ledger.py:1424). Line 1061-1063 states this explicitly: "abstraction is INTENTIONALLY not weighted ... It stays as an advisory metric + flag only." The score is driven by diff_size(35), nesting(30), net_growth(20), fan_out(8), blob(7). A 3-line change (tiny diff, low nesting, low net growth) scores near 100 → SIMPLE, never OVERBUILT; the factory smell only emits an advisory flag (qa_ledger.py:1444-1447), never lowers the band. OVERBUILT is reached by large/sprawling diffs, not by a single small factory abstraction.
discrepancies.delta: The command invocation (`simplicity-check --from-git`) and the OVERBUILT verdict both exist exactly as stated, so the sentence is technically defensible at the surface. However the chosen EXAMPLE is false: the tool cannot flag a 3-line DiscountStrategyFactory as OVERBUILT. Abstraction/factory detection is advisory-only (unweighted, qa_ledger.py:1061-1066); it produces a flag but never moves the score below the 65 OVERBUILT floor. A 3-line diff scores near-perfect on every WEIGHTED dimension and lands SIMPLE. OVERBUILT is driven by size/nesting/growth/fan-out/blob, so the doc creates the false impression that adding a small speculative abstraction triggers OVERBUILT, when in reality it triggers at most an advisory YAGNI flag while the verdict stays SIMPLE.
discrepancies.fix: Change the example to one that actually drives OVERBUILT via a weighted dimension, e.g. "simplicity-check --from-git → OVERBUILT: +900 added lines / net growth +600 over budget" or "a single +250-line hunk across 40 files." If the intent is to showcase the factory/YAGNI detection, phrase it as an advisory flag rather than the verdict: "simplicity-check flags a DiscountStrategyFactory added for 3 lines with a YAGNI/speculative-generality advisory (verdict stays SIMPLE — abstraction count is not weighted into the band)."

discrepancies.claim: /discovery is for when you have an idea but not a shape; /adr-refine is for when the shape is known and only the edges need drawing.
discrepancies.doc_quote: Run /discovery when you have an idea but not a shape; run /adr-refine when the shape is known and only the edges need drawing.
discrepancies.code_does: discovery/SKILL.md:2-19 is the "front of the methodology for greenfield work," takes "a general idea" (trigger: "solo tengo la idea, no sé el cómo todavía"), and its explicit job is "You bring the shape" — proposing domain model, API surface and architecture options one question at a time. adr-refine/SKILL.md:3,15-19 does NOT require a known shape: its stated input is also "a rough idea," and it defines itself as "NOT a generator... an interrogator that distills." Its Phase A agenda (adr-refine/SKILL.md:37-64) forces explicit decisions on the big implicit choices — sync vs async, storage, protocol, idempotency, transactional boundaries, architecture — each with at least one considered alternative, which is shape-level work, not edge-drawing. The real distinguishing axis in the docs is propose-the-shape (discovery) vs. interrogate-and-distill/converge-on-an-objective-exit-criterion (adr-refine, lines 22-76), and greenfield vs. pre-coding refinement — not "no shape yet" vs "shape known, only edges left."
discrepancies.delta: The discovery half of the claim is accurate. The adr-refine half is not supported: the doc says adr-refine also starts from "a rough idea" (adr-refine/SKILL.md:3,17) and its interview forces the big architectural/implicit decisions with alternatives (lines 44-64) — i.e. it still shapes the system, it does not assume the shape is known with only edges to draw. The claim collapses the genuine distinction (propose vs. interrogate-and-converge; greenfield vs. pre-coding) into an input-maturity dichotomy the docs never state.
discrepancies.fix: Reframe on the axis the SKILL.md files actually use: "Run /discovery for greenfield work when you have an idea and need Claude to PROPOSE the system shape (domain model, API surface, architecture) one decision at a time; run /adr-refine when you have a rough idea and want Claude to INTERROGATE it — surfacing implicit decisions and failure modes and converging on an objective exit criterion — before coding." Both accept a rough/general idea; do not imply adr-refine requires a known shape with only edges to draw.

discrepancies.claim: A CONSTITUTION violation logs a BLOCKER that caps readiness at ≤65 and blocks convergence.
discrepancies.doc_quote: A violation logs a BLOCKER: caps readiness ≤65, blocks convergence.
discrepancies.code_does: The engine has NO "CONSTITUTION" concept at all — the string never appears in qa_ledger.py (grep: no matches). The ≤65 cap is `DEFAULT_CAPS["blocker_critical"]=65` (qa_ledger.py:796), applied in cmd_readiness only when aggregated static-analysis severity counts have BLOCKER+CRITICAL > 0 (qa_ledger.py:970-972; per-repo at 888-890). "BLOCKER" is a static-analysis SEVERITY level (PMD priority 1 -> "BLOCKER", qa_ledger.py:282; SEVERITY_ORDER at 277), aggregated from each linter's severity_counts (_gate_open_and_sev, 835-843) — not a "logged violation." Convergence (cmd_converged / _converged, qa_ledger.py:619-672) is decided purely by: last agent cycle has zero GATED findings, zero files changed, green tests, and every linter's latest static-gate run has zero GATED findings (649-655). It never inspects severity labels, so a BLOCKER-severity finding does not "block convergence"; only gated-finding COUNTS matter. Both cmd_converged (labeled "ADVISORY", line 659) and readiness are advisory — the cap only ceilings a readiness score, it does not hard-block anything.
discrepancies.fix: Rewrite to match the code. There is no CONSTITUTION mechanism. Accurate statement: "When any static-gate run reports findings at BLOCKER or CRITICAL severity, the aggregate readiness score is capped at 65 (readiness_caps.blocker_critical). Severity does not affect convergence — convergence (advisory) requires zero GATED findings and green tests, regardless of severity." If a CONSTITUTION-violation feature is intended, it must be built in code first (fix_target then becomes both).

discrepancies.claim: Change classification uses five profiles A–E with these minimum gates: A Low = build + relevant test; B Normal = tests + static + review; C Critical = unit+integration+security+rollback; D Multi-system = contract tests + versioning; E Legacy = characterization + no-regression.
discrepancies.doc_quote: A · Low | minor UI / config | build + relevant test ... B · Normal | local feature / bugfix | tests + static + review ... C · Critical | payments / security | unit+integration+security+rollback ... D · Multi-system | public API / events | contract tests + versioning ... E · Legacy | refactor / migration | characterization + no-regression
discrepancies.code_does: The kit has no five-profile (A–E) change-classification system. qa_ledger.py only defines a finding SEVERITY scale — `SEVERITY_ORDER = ["INFO","LOW","MEDIUM","HIGH","CRITICAL","BLOCKER"]` (qa_ledger.py:277) — plus a `severity_gate` default of BLOCKER/CRITICAL/HIGH (qa_ledger.py:542); that is issue triage, not per-change profile selection. There is no code path that classifies a change into A/B/C/D/E or maps a profile to a minimum gate set. The only "risk profile" mentions are two casual prose references in SKILL.md ("tighten per risk profile" line 116; "risk profile C+/E" line 190) that never define A–E rows or their gates, plus a "Legacy baseline" bullet in templates/CLAUDE.md:26 and a golden/characterization invariant in CONSTITUTION.md:70-81. The exact table rows quoted (minor UI/config → build+relevant test; local feature/bugfix → tests+static+review; payments/security → unit+integration+security+rollback; public API/events → contract tests+versioning; refactor/migration → characterization+no-regression) appear nowhere in qa_ledger.py, SKILL.md, CONSTITUTION.md, CLAUDE.md, or dev-loop.config.json.
discrepancies.delta: The doc presents a concrete, authoritative five-row A–E profile table with change types and per-profile minimum gates as if it were an implemented classification mechanism. The code implements none of it: no profile enum, no change-type→profile mapping, no profile→gate mapping. The kit only has (1) a finding-severity gate (unrelated to change classification) and (2) undefined ad-hoc "C+/E" prose references. The doc oversells a governance table that has no backing logic or even a defining spec in the kit.
discrepancies.fix: Either (a) demote the doc's A–E table to an explicitly aspirational/advisory heuristic and stop implying it drives gate selection, or (b) implement it: add a defined A–E profile table (in CONSTITUTION.md or a config block) and wire qa_ledger.py to accept a `--profile` and select the corresponding minimum gates. Also reconcile the stray "C+/E" references in SKILL.md:116,190 with whichever definition becomes canonical, since those letters are currently used without any defining table.

Golden testing is implemented by the characterize skill + qa_ledger.py golden-diff (cmd_golden_diff, qa_ledger.py:1904–1952) and is triggered mechanically by the presence of *.received/*.approved fixtures — with no fixtures it PASSES ("sin fixtures .received — nada que comparar", qa_ledger.py:1941), so it is not "mandatory" and is never conditioned on a profile. discrepancies.delta: Doc invents two structures that do not exist in the code: (1) a "Profile E" that makes golden testing "mandatory" — the code has no profile→golden coupling, and golden-diff is a no-op when no fixtures exist; and (2) a cross-reference to "play 08," which does not exist anywhere in the kit. The only real "Profile E" mention gates the optional rebuild test, not golden testing. The baseline-before-touching guidance is real but attached to migration work, not to Profile E.
discrepancies.fix: Remove the invented Profile E / play 08 coupling. Either (a) drop the sentence, or (b) rewrite to match reality: "Before any migration/modernization, baseline the old behavior with the characterize skill and let golden-diff (qa_ledger.py golden-diff) byte-compare .received vs the human-approved .approved. Note that golden-diff only runs when fixtures exist — it is not auto-mandatory. Separately, risk profile C+/E may trigger the optional Phase 5b rebuild test (dev-loop/SKILL.md)." Also either define the A–E risk-profile taxonomy somewhere real or stop citing it, and remove the "play 08" reference since no play system exists.

discrepancies.claim: The 'Ralph Wiggum loop' is the failure mode where the agent fires the done token too early; only an objective gate closes it, never an opinion.
discrepancies.doc_quote: The Ralph Wiggum loop — the agent fires the "done" token too early. Only an objective gate closes it; never an opinion.
discrepancies.code_does: The convergence check IS objective/mechanical: `_converged()` (qa_ledger.py:632-655) returns clean only when the last agent cycle has zero gated findings, zero files changed, green tests, AND every latest static-gate run is clean — no opinion enters that function. HOWEVER, this gate is explicitly ADVISORY, not authoritative: `cmd_converged` docstring says "ADVISORY" (qa_ledger.py:660) and dev-loop/SKILL.md:156 states "End-of-cycle checks (advisory — you make the final call)". SKILL.md:168 then has the agent decide to leave the loop. So in the real design the objective gate INFORMS an opinion-based termination decision; it does not itself close the loop. There is also no "Ralph Wiggum" concept and no "done token" mechanism anywhere in the kit (grep across the whole tree returns nothing).
discrepancies.delta: The claim's spirit — decisions should be grounded in objective gate signals, not vibes — matches the code's intent (the gate is genuinely opinion-free). But the absolute "Only an objective gate closes it; never an opinion" contradicts the implementation: the convergence gate is labeled ADVISORY and the human/agent "make[s] the final call" (SKILL.md:156, qa_ledger.py:660). The gate constrains and informs the closing decision; it does not autonomously close the loop. The evocative "Ralph Wiggum loop"/"done token" framing is a doc-only rhetorical label with no corresponding mechanism in code.
discrepancies.fix: Soften the absolute wording to match the advisory design, e.g.: "The Ralph Wiggum loop — the agent calls it 'done' too early. Ground that call in the objective convergence gate (zero gated findings, zero files changed, green tests, clean static gate), not a vibe. The gate is advisory: it must be satisfied before you close the loop, but you still make the final call." Avoid claiming the gate alone closes the loop or that opinion is never involved.

discrepancies.claim: qa_ledger.py reads real files for its evidence: coverage from a coverage report (e.g. jacoco.xml / lcov); tests from test result XML (e.g. JUnit / surefire); static from linters, type-checker, security scanner; LOC from its own count using stdlib.
discrepancies.doc_quote:
coverage  ← coverage report (e.g. jacoco.xml / lcov)
tests     ← test result XML (e.g. JUnit / surefire)
static    ← linters · type-checker · security scanner
LOC       ← its own count (stdlib)
discrepancies.code_does: coverage: maven_coverage parses jacoco.xml (target/site/jacoco[-aggregate]/jacoco.xml) via ET.parse and flutter_coverage sums LF/LH from coverage/lcov.info — qa_ledger.py:106-160. tests: maven_test_count parses surefire/failsafe TEST-*.xml (JUnit format) with ET.parse — qa_ledger.py:170-193; BUT flutter_test_count does NOT read any result XML, it statically greps `test(`/`testWidgets(` declarations and self-flags `approximate: True` — qa_ledger.py:196-220. static: ingest-gate parses Checkstyle (parse_checkstyle:341), PMD (parse_pmd:357), and SpotBugs, splitting FindSecBugs/SECURITY findings out as the security scanner (parse_spotbugs:377-402); no type-checker parser exists anywhere in the file. LOC: count_loc uses os.walk + non-blank-line count, stdlib only — qa_ledger.py:244-270.
discrepancies.delta: Three of four rows are exactly right (coverage=jacoco/lcov, LOC=stdlib count, static=linters+security-scanner). Two overstatements: (1) "static ← ... type-checker ..." has NO code backing — the ingest-gate parses only Checkstyle/PMD/SpotBugs/FindSecBugs (linters + a security scanner); nothing type-checks (no mypy/tsc/etc.). (2) "tests ← test result XML (e.g. JUnit / surefire)" is true only for maven repos; flutter test counts are a STATIC source-grep approximation (flutter_test_count), not parsed from any result XML, and the code itself flags them approximate.
discrepancies.fix: Drop "type-checker" from the static row (or add an actual type-checker parser if intended) since no type-checker is ingested. Qualify the tests row: "tests ← test result XML for maven (JUnit/surefire); flutter is a best-effort static count of test()/testWidgets() declarations, flagged approximate."

discrepancies.claim: Fact-reading gates block while prose-guessing gates only advise: golden-diff (reads bytes vs .approved) BLOCKS; pit-check (reads mutation XML) BLOCKS; gate-check (reads diff structure) BLOCKS; static gate (reads 4 linters, normalized) BLOCKS; spec-check (reads prose heuristic) ADVISES.
discrepancies.doc_quote: golden-diff | bytes vs .approved | BLOCKS ... pit-check | mutation XML | BLOCKS ... gate-check | diff structure | BLOCKS ... static gate | 4 linters, normalized | BLOCKS ... spec-check | prose heuristic | ADVISES
discrepancies.code_does: Exit-code behavior in qa_ledger.py: golden-diff BLOCKS (sys.exit(0 if passed else 1) at :1938/:1952, byte-compares .received vs .approved at :1919-1926); pit-check BLOCKS (sys.exit(0 if passed else 1) at :1598/:1616, reads mutation XML at :1582); gate-check BLOCKS (sys.exit(1 if blocker else 0) at :1712/:1733, reads git-diff structure at :1653); spec-check ADVISES (fail = args.strict and n_find>0 at :1859, sys.exit(1 if fail else 0) at :1864/:1881 — advisory unless --strict). But the "static gate" = cmd_ingest_gate (:534), which reads the 4 linters (Checkstyle/PMD/SpotBugs/FindSecBugs, :547-563), has NO sys.exit(1): it returns at :618 or falls through to end, always exit 0. It only records static-gate steps into the ledger that feed the readiness KPI (dev-loop.config.json static_gate weight 20 / static_gate_zero_at 10). Within this engine it advises/records; it does not block by exit code.
discrepancies.delta: 4 of 5 cells match exactly (golden-diff/pit-check/gate-check BLOCK; spec-check ADVISES). The 5th cell is wrong for the named subcommand: the doc says the "static gate (ingest-gate)" BLOCKS, but ingest-gate never exits non-zero — it is a recorder feeding readiness, not an exit-code blocker. Any actual per-severity blocking of the 4 linters happens in the Maven java-qa-gate build, not in qa_ledger.py. The thesis "fact-reading gates block" is a category claim; ingest-gate reads facts (linter XML) yet does NOT block, which itself weakens the tidy fact-vs-prose dichotomy the doc draws.
discrepancies.fix: Change the static-gate row from BLOCKS to something like "static gate | 4 linters, normalized | RECORDS (feeds readiness; blocking is in the Maven java-qa-gate, not qa_ledger)". Or drop ingest-gate from the fact-reading-blocks list, since within qa_ledger.py the true exit-code blockers are golden-diff, pit-check, and gate-check (plus spec-check --strict). Keep the golden-diff/pit-check/gate-check=BLOCK and spec-check=ADVISE cells as-is; they are accurate.

discrepancies.doc_quote: Fix first. But minimum evidence (what changed, how to roll back) + a retroactive SPEC/ADR are due within 24h.

Searches for "Fix first", "24h", "24 hours", "retroactive", "hotfix", "p0", "emergency", "bypass", "escape valve", and "roll back" across the dev-loop and discovery SKILL.md files, the CONSTITUTION and CLAUDE.md templates, and the whole dev-loop-kit tree return no matching methodology text (only unrelated substring hits like `p0`/`p1` variables in qa_ledger.py:1233 and "rollback" invariant checklist items). discrepancies.delta: The doc claims a concrete escape valve for p0 hotfixes: fix immediately, then supply minimum evidence (what changed + rollback) plus a retroactive SPEC/ADR within 24h. Neither the escape valve, the 24-hour deadline, the "minimum evidence" package, nor the retroactive SPEC/ADR requirement appears anywhere in the actual skills, templates, or config. discrepancies.claim: Setup installs Claude Code via native installer (curl install.sh on mac/linux/wsl, irm install.ps1 on windows), copies dev-loop-kit/.claude/skills/* to ~/.claude/skills/, adds the gentleman scoop bucket, installs gentle-ai, and runs claude --version && claude doctor.
discrepancies.doc_quote:
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash   # mac/linux/wsl
irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex          # windows
cp -r dev-loop-kit/.claude/skills/* ~/.claude/skills/
scoop bucket add gentleman https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/scoop-bucket
scoop install gentle-ai                          # the step everyone misses
claude --version && claude doctor
discrepancies.code_does: WORKBENCH.md §2 installs Claude Code via the official native installer — `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash` (mac/linux/wsl) and `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex` (windows) — plus npm/brew/CMD alternatives, then verifies with `claude --version` and `claude doctor` (WORKBENCH.md §2 "Verificar" line and §9). §5 copies skills globally with exactly `cp -r dev-loop-kit/.claude/skills/* ~/.claude/skills/`. discrepancies.delta: Three of the six claimed steps match the docs verbatim (install.sh, install.ps1, the skills cp, and the claude --version && claude doctor verify). But the two scoop steps — `scoop bucket add gentleman https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/scoop-bucket` and `scoop install gentle-ai` — are fabricated: they appear nowhere in WORKBENCH.md, README.md, workbench-doctor.sh, or any file in the kit. discrepancies.doc_quote: Gotcha: settings.json hardcodes C:\Users\…. The bootstrap tokenizes the path on export and rewrites it on import.

Hook wiring (block-approved-writes.ps1) must be pasted into your own .claude/settings.json by hand — the agent can't do it due to the self-modification guardrail — and you substitute your absolute kit path into the `<path>` placeholder yourself. discrepancies.claim: Command reference: /adr-refine = polish a decision's edges.
discrepancies.doc_quote: /adr-refine | polish a decision's edges.
discrepancies.code_does: adr-refine/SKILL.md:3-13 defines the skill as turning a rough idea into a development-ready ADR set + ACCEPTANCE.md by running a structured Socratic INTERVIEW (problem, implicit decisions, failure modes, constraints, DoD, dependencies), refusing to emit artifacts until gaps close, then distilling into docs/adr/ADR-NNN.md. Lines 21-23 make the intent explicit: "Interrogate, don't agree... A refinement where you agreed with everything failed." It is the "front-half counterpart to dev-loop" — a pre-coding spec/interrogation generator, not a polisher of an existing decision.
discrepancies.delta: Doc's gloss "polish a decision's edges" frames the tool as lightly smoothing an already-made decision. The actual skill takes a ROUGH IDEA (not a finished decision) and CREATES the ADR set via an adversarial Socratic interview that explicitly refuses to just agree/validate. "Polish edges" connotes gentle validation — the opposite of the skill's "interrogate, don't agree; surface the holes" mandate — and omits that it generates the artifacts.
discrepancies.fix: Change the gloss to reflect interrogation + generation, e.g. "/adr-refine | interrogate a rough idea into a development-ready ADR set."

discrepancies.claim: Command reference: /dev-loop = plan → coverage → build → QA loop → integration.
discrepancies.doc_quote: /dev-loop | plan → coverage → build → QA loop → integration.
discrepancies.code_does: SKILL.md defines an 11-phase pipeline: Phase 0 Plan (SKILL.md:49), Phase 1 Coverage gate → characterization (SKILL.md:62), Phase 2 Build (SKILL.md:78), Phase 2b Simplicity gate (SKILL.md:102), Phase 3 QA loop (SKILL.md:119), Phase 4 Integration/contract (SKILL.md:171), Phase 5 Verify/coverage generation (SKILL.md:178), Phase 5b Rebuild test (SKILL.md:190), Phase 6 PR/stop-at-merge (SKILL.md:210), Phase 7 Smoke list (SKILL.md:216), Phase 8 Docs + retrospective (SKILL.md:221).

But the real pipeline continues past integration through Verify (Phase 5), PR/stop-at-merge (Phase 6), Smoke (Phase 7) and Docs/retrospective (Phase 8), and it also skips Phase 2b Simplicity gate. discrepancies.fix: Extend the one-liner to reflect the full pipeline, e.g. "/dev-loop | plan → coverage → build → simplicity → QA loop → integration → verify → PR (stop at merge) → docs", or add a trailing "→ …" / "(through PR/merge gate + docs)" to signal it continues past integration.

discrepancies.claim: The pipeline flows SPEC + ACCEPTANCE (/discovery) → dev-loop (build + tests) → /qa (gates CI) → human gate (reads the diff) → ship.
discrepancies.doc_quote: SPEC + ACCEPTANCE /discovery … dev-loop build + tests … /qa gates CI … human gate reads the diff · ALWAYS … ship
discrepancies.code_does: The real pipeline (discovery/SKILL.md:126) is: `/discovery` (idea → spec package: CONTEXT/SPEC/ADR/ACCEPTANCE) → `/dev-loop` (build + QA + evidence) → human gate. There is NO separate `/qa` skill or step: the installed skills are adr-refine, characterize, dev-loop, discovery, reverse-discovery, sys-doc (no `qa`). QA is Phase 3 *inside* dev-loop (dev-loop/SKILL.md:119-169), driven by qa_ledger.py (a measurement engine, not a skill) whose subcommands are init/snapshot/check-coverage/log-step/ingest-gate/converged/oscillation/escalate/summary/readiness/rebuild/simplicity-check/pit-check/gate-check/spec-check/golden-diff. dev-loop does NOT gate CI — Phase 6 (dev-loop/SKILL.md:210-214) says "Open the PR(s). Confirm CI is green. STOP." (it confirms external CI, it does not gate it), and its local gates (check-coverage, converged, simplicity-check) are advisory exit codes. The human gate is the real blocker: dev-loop/SKILL.md:32 "Stop at merge … The human owns the merge gate", and templates/CLAUDE.md:33 + CONSTITUTION.md:32 confirm "human gate siempre / ALWAYS".
discrepancies.delta: The claim inserts `/qa` as a discrete pipeline stage between dev-loop and the human gate, and says it "gates CI". In the code QA is not a separate stage — it is Phase 3 embedded inside `/dev-loop` (build, tests, and the severity-gated review loop all live in the same skill). And nothing "gates CI": dev-loop's Phase 6 opens the PR and *confirms* CI is already green, then stops for the human. The accurate parts: SPEC+ACCEPTANCE come from /discovery, dev-loop does build+tests, the human gate reads the diff and is ALWAYS present, then ship.
discrepancies.fix: Reword to match the documented flow and drop the phantom `/qa` stage: "SPEC + ACCEPTANCE (/discovery) → dev-loop (build + tests + severity-gated QA loop via qa_ledger, confirms CI green) → human gate reads the diff · ALWAYS → ship." If a distinct `/qa` label is wanted for narrative, footnote that QA is Phase 3 *inside* dev-loop, not a separate skill, and that dev-loop confirms CI rather than gating it.

discrepancies.claim: Inside /qa, the BLOCK-tier gates that read facts are golden-diff, pit-check, gate-check, readiness/rebuild, and simplicity caps.
discrepancies.doc_quote: BLOCK · read FACTS … golden-diff … pit-check … gate-check … readiness / rebuild … simplicity caps
discrepancies.code_does: The doc claim's exact source is CHANGELOG-1.2.5.md:22 ("BLOQUEAN (leen hechos): golden-diff, pit-check, gate-check, readiness/rebuild, caps de simplicity"). Four of the five named items are genuine fact-reading gates that block via non-zero exit: golden-diff byte-compares .received vs .approved and exits 1 on divergence (qa_ledger.py:1889 comment "diverged = BLOCKER (exit 1)", exit at :1938/:1952); pit-check exits 1 when mutation score < min-score (:1587,:1616); gate-check emits verdict BLOCKER and exits 1 (:1701,:1712,:1733); rebuild exits 1 unless verdict==COVERS (:1262,:1273); simplicity-check numeric caps exit 1 on OVERBUILT (:1490,:1514) and per CHANGELOG:13-14 the numeric caps (lines/files/nesting) still gate while the abstraction regex was demoted to advisory. The outlier is readiness: cmd_readiness (:986–:1022) computes a weighted 0–100 score with hard caps that only LOWER the number (tests red→≤35, BLOCKER/CRITICAL→≤65, :968–:977, :237–:238) and always exits 0 — there is no sys.exit(1) path. It is a KPI reporter, and SKILL.md:156 even labels the end-of-cycle checks as "advisory — you make the final call." So grouping "readiness" under "BLOQUEAN"/BLOCK alongside true exit-code gates conflates a non-blocking score with actual blocking gates; the "caps" gate the human's release decision, not the script's exit status.
discrepancies.delta: The claim/doc lists five items as gates that BLOCK (bloquean). Four block by non-zero exit code (golden-diff, pit-check, gate-check, rebuild, plus simplicity numeric caps). But "readiness" does NOT block: cmd_readiness always exits 0 and only emits a capped 0–100 KPI score; its hard caps lower the number, they do not return a failing exit. The doc bundles it as "readiness/rebuild" under the blocking header, implying readiness itself gates when only rebuild does.
discrepancies.fix: Split "readiness/rebuild" in the BLOQUEAN line: keep rebuild (and golden-diff, pit-check, gate-check, simplicity numeric caps) as the exit-code gates that BLOCK, and describe readiness separately as a fact-derived KPI whose hard caps ceiling the score (informing the human release decision) rather than a gate that returns a blocking exit. E.g. "BLOQUEAN (exit): golden-diff, pit-check, gate-check, rebuild, caps numéricos de simplicity. INFORMA (KPI con caps duros, no exit): readiness."

discrepancies.claim: Advisory gates report but do not block, and require --strict to gate.
discrepancies.doc_quote: report, don't block (--strict to gate)
discrepancies.code_does: spec-check IS advisory-by-default and requires --strict to gate: `fail = args.strict and n_find > 0` and `sys.exit(1 if fail else 0)` (qa_ledger.py:1859, 1864, 1881); verdict is "ADVISORY"/"OK" and prints "spec-check es ADVISORY (--strict para gatear)" (line 1878). --strict is registered only for spec-check (line 2117) and gate-check (line 2107). BUT simplicity-check — which the CHECK-AGAINST explicitly names — has NO --strict flag (argparse ps2, lines 2069-2087 register no --strict) and BLOCKS by default: `sys.exit(0 if verdict != "OVERBUILT" else 1)` (lines 1490 and 1514). An OVERBUILT diff exits 1 with no flag. gate-check similarly blocks by default on hard signals regardless of --strict: `blocker = hard > 0 or (args.strict and soft > 0)` (line 1700) — --strict only escalates SOFT flags.
discrepancies.delta: The doc string "report, don't block (--strict to gate)" correctly describes spec-check (and the soft-flag path of gate-check), but the claim scopes this semantic to simplicity-check as well. simplicity-check accepts no --strict flag and hard-blocks (exit 1) on OVERBUILT by default (lines 1490/1514) — it is a blocking Reduce gate, not an advisory one. gate-check also hard-blocks by default on removed tests/thresholds; --strict only adds soft-flag gating (line 1700). So "advisory gates ... require --strict to gate" is accurate for spec-check but false for simplicity-check.
discrepancies.fix: Scope the "report, don't block (--strict to gate)" phrasing to spec-check (and the soft-flag path of gate-check) only. State clearly that simplicity-check is a blocking gate (exit 1 on OVERBUILT, no --strict flag) and that gate-check blocks by default on hard signals with --strict only escalating soft flags. Do not group simplicity-check under advisory/--strict semantics.

discrepancies.claim: readiness/rebuild reads test/coverage reports and COVERS/DIVERGE and BLOCKS.
discrepancies.doc_quote: readiness / rebuild | test/coverage reports; COVERS/DIVERGE | BLOCKS
discrepancies.code_does: The doc row groups `readiness` and `rebuild` under one set of attributes (reads "test/coverage reports"; tokens "COVERS/DIVERGE"; effect "BLOCKS"). This is accurate for `rebuild` but wrong for `readiness` on 2 of 3 attributes. `rebuild`: `_rebuild_compare` reads test reports (qa_ledger.py:1197-1211), coverage (1223-1230) and acceptance/LOC; verdict banded by `REBUILD_BANDS = [(90,"COVERS"),(70,"PARTIAL"),(0,"DIVERGE")]` (line 1053, printed line 1263); and it BLOCKS via `sys.exit(0 if verdict == "COVERS" else 1)` (lines 1262, 1273). `readiness`: DOES read test/coverage (calls `coverage()` at 873/928 and `_tests_red` at 885/968), but its status comes from `_band` using `BANDS = [(95,"READY"),(80,"RELEASE CANDIDATE"),(50,"IN PROGRESS"),(0,"NOT READY")]` (line 798) — it emits READY/NOT READY, NOT COVERS/DIVERGE (those belong exclusively to `rebuild`). And `cmd_readiness` never calls `sys.exit(1)` — it only `return`s (line 1004) or falls through after printing, so it does NOT BLOCK; the code comment at line 790-793 frames it as an advisory state KPI, not a gate.
discrepancies.delta: The doc attributes COVERS/DIVERGE tokens and BLOCKS behavior to BOTH subcommands. In reality only `rebuild` uses COVERS/DIVERGE and only `rebuild` blocks (non-zero exit). `readiness` uses READY/RELEASE CANDIDATE/IN PROGRESS/NOT READY tokens and always exits 0 (advisory, never blocks). The only fully-correct shared attribute is "reads test/coverage reports".
discrepancies.fix: Split the row. `rebuild` | reads test/coverage/acceptance reports | COVERS/PARTIAL/DIVERGE | BLOCKS (exit 1 unless COVERS). `readiness` | reads test/coverage reports + ledger gate/convergence state | READY/RELEASE CANDIDATE/IN PROGRESS/NOT READY (with hard caps) | advisory, never blocks (always exits 0).

discrepancies.claim: simplicity-check reads numeric caps (lines/files/nesting) treated as fact and BLOCKS.
discrepancies.doc_quote: simplicity-check | numeric caps (lines/files/nesting) = fact | BLOCKS
discrepancies.code_does: simplicity-check reads numeric caps as fact but gates exit code on a weighted composite score (< 65 = OVERBUILT = exit 1), not on individual cap breaches; a single cap being exceeded emits an advisory flag and lowers one weighted dimension, and usually does NOT block (qa_ledger.py:1411-1436, 1467-1514).
discrepancies.delta: Doc: "numeric caps (lines/files/nesting) = fact | BLOCKS" implies exceeding a cap blocks. Code: caps are inputs to a WEIGHTED composite score (diff_size 35, nesting 30, net_growth 20, fan_out 8, blob 7); blocking (exit 1) happens only when that composite < 65 (verdict OVERBUILT), not when any single cap is breached. Concrete: nesting=8 vs cap 4 zeroes the nesting dimension (weight 30) but score = (35+0+20+8+7)=70 → ACCEPTABLE → exit 0, no block. files_changed (fan_out, weight 8) can be breached with almost no blocking effect. "lines/files/nesting" as the blocking trigger is inaccurate — the composite is.
discrepancies.fix: Reword to: "simplicity-check | numeric caps feed a WEIGHTED composite score, treated as fact | BLOCKS only when composite score < 65 (OVERBUILT); a single cap breach flags but does not block." Do not imply that exceeding lines/files/nesting caps individually blocks.

discrepancies.claim: Fact-reading BLOCK gates are meant to run in CI and be forgotten.
discrepancies.doc_quote: Hard exit 1, break the chain. Objective, cheap, no opinion. Run in CI and forget them.
discrepancies.code_does: The kit's real distilled rule is "fact-reading gates block, prose-guessers advise" (qa_ledger.py:1744) — the "BLOCK gate / exit 1 / objective, cheap, no opinion" half is accurate. But the fact-reading gates are driven INSIDE the interactive dev-loop by the agent at named phases, not parked in CI: simplicity-check is Phase 2b run before the loop and its OVERBUILT exit-1 means "reduce first and re-run — do not carry it into the QA loop" (SKILL.md:113-116); check-coverage runs at the pre phase (SKILL.md:66-68); ingest-gate feeds the per-cycle QA loop with severity caps (SKILL.md:138-148); golden-diff is a loop-time byte-comparison capture/compare (qa_ledger.py:1886-1889,1904). The kit's actual CI/merge contract is human-owned: "Stop at merge... The human owns the merge gate" (SKILL.md:32-33) and "Open the PR(s). Confirm CI is green. STOP." (SKILL.md:213-214). CI appears only as (a) a final green-check the agent confirms before handing off and (b) an OPTIONAL periodic host for rebuild/simplicity (SKILL.md:190; README:163,189) — never as "set up the block gates in CI and forget them." Also note the exact quoted DOC string does not appear verbatim anywhere in the kit.
discrepancies.delta: DOC says the fact-reading BLOCK gates are meant to "Run in CI and forget them" (fire-and-forget CI wiring). The code invokes those gates interactively during the agent-driven dev-loop (Phase 2b simplicity, pre-phase coverage, per-cycle static-gate ingestion, golden-diff capture), and treats CI as a human-owned final stop ("Stop at merge", "Confirm CI is green. STOP"), with CI hosting only OPTIONAL periodic rebuild/simplicity checks. The gates are loop-time convergence inputs, not set-and-forget CI checks. (The accurate half — objective, cheap, exit 1, no opinion — matches; the "run in CI and forget" half does not.)
discrepancies.fix: Reword to reflect the actual operating model: these gates are objective, cheap, exit-1 fact checks the agent runs at fixed points INSIDE the dev-loop (simplicity before the loop, coverage at pre, static-gate ingestion each cycle, golden-diff on capture) to feed convergence — and CI is a human-owned final stop the agent confirms, not a place the gates are parked and ignored. E.g.: "Hard exit 1, break the chain. Objective, cheap, no opinion — run them at their phase in the loop; the human owns the merge/CI gate at the end."

discrepancies.claim: In the developer day-to-day, fact gates live in CI and not in the dev's face; the flow is spec → code (agent) → /qa in CI running golden-diff, pit-check, gate-check, readiness with exit 0/1, then the human reads the diff and ships.
discrepancies.doc_quote: # fact gates live in CI, NOT in the dev's face … spec → code (agent) → /qa in CI: golden-diff · pit-check · gate-check · readiness # exit 0/1 → the human READS the diff → ship
discrepancies.code_does: The kit exposes ONE orchestrator invocation, `/dev-loop` (README.md:107; dev-loop/SKILL.md), not `/qa` — no `/qa` command exists anywhere in the kit. The gates are stdlib-Python subcommands the AGENT runs INLINE during the loop, in the dev's face, not in CI: there are zero CI/workflow files (no *.yml/*.yaml in the kit), and the skill is explicitly a human-in-the-loop orchestrator that 'stops at the merge gate for human approval' (SKILL.md:8-9,32; Phase 6 lines 210-214). The four named gates are not one bundle: simplicity-check is Phase 2b (line 109), gate-check/pit-check are Phase-3 gates, golden-diff is the approval gate, and readiness is a Phase-8 KPI (lines 228-233). golden-diff (qa_ledger.py:1938,1952), pit-check (1598,1616) and gate-check (1712,1733) do exit 0/1, but `cmd_readiness` (qa_ledger.py:906-1004) only prints a 0..100 score/JSON and returns normally — it has NO sys.exit(0/1), so 'readiness with exit 0/1' is false; it is a scoring KPI, not a pass/fail gate.
discrepancies.delta: The doc claims (a) a `/qa` command — none exists, only `/dev-loop`; (b) gates 'live in CI, NOT in the dev's face' — there is no CI in the kit; gates run inline in the agent-driven loop and the flow is deliberately human-in-the-loop, stopping at the merge gate; (c) golden-diff · pit-check · gate-check · readiness run together as one CI step — they are spread across Phases 2b/3/6/8; (d) 'readiness with exit 0/1' — readiness does not gate, it prints a score and always exits 0.
discrepancies.fix: Rewrite to reflect reality: 'spec → code → `/dev-loop`: agent runs the QA loop inline (simplicity/gate/pit/golden gates exit 0/1, readiness is a 0..100 KPI), converges, then STOPS at the merge gate → human reviews and merges.' Drop the `/qa` name, drop the CI-not-in-your-face framing (the loop is explicitly in the dev's face and human-gated), and stop listing readiness as an exit-0/1 gate.

discrepancies.claim: Cross-file consistency judgment goes to a non-correlated checker — a different model family, not another instance of the same one.
discrepancies.doc_quote: it goes to the non-correlated checker (a different model family, not another instance of the same one). Computational within the file; inferential cross-file.
discrepancies.code_does: The kit defines the non-correlated checker as "otra familia/perfil" (another FAMILY **or** PROFILE), not strictly a different model family. See CONSTITUTION.md:67 ("el checker es no-correlacionado con el maker (otra familia/perfil)") and CONSTITUTION.md:97-98 ("se exige además un checker no-correlacionado con el maker (distinta familia/perfil) — eso es proceso, no código"). The routing half is right: qa_ledger.py:1739-1742 says spec-check does the COMPUTATIONAL checks in-file and defers CONSISTENCY (contradictory clauses) as a "semantic/inferential check for the non-correlated checker" (echoed at qa_ledger.py:1878). Note also the doc's own citations are wrong: there is no judgment-day/SKILL.md in this kit, and "spec-check" is a subcommand of qa_ledger.py, not a sys-doc feature — sys-doc/SKILL.md (84 lines) contains none of the terms checker/inferential/computational/consistency.
discrepancies.delta: Doc: "a different model family, not another instance of the same one." Code: "otra familia/PERFIL" / "distinta familia/PERFIL" — the "/perfil" disjunction explicitly permits the SAME family running under a different profile/persona to act as the checker. The doc drops the "/perfil" branch and adds the exclusion "not another instance of the same one," which the code never states and in fact contradicts (a different-profile instance of the same family is allowed). The code also frames this as PROCESS, not code ("eso es proceso, no código", CONSTITUTION.md:98) and never says "model" — it says agent family/profile. The "computational within the file; inferential cross-file" clause is accurate. Citations to judgment-day/SKILL.md and sys-doc/spec-check do not resolve to anything in the kit.
discrepancies.fix: Change the doc to match the code's disjunction: "it goes to the non-correlated checker — a different agent family OR at least a different profile/persona of the same one — so the reviewer is not correlated with the maker. This is a process rule, not enforced by code. Computational checks stay within the file; consistency (inferential) crosses to the checker." Drop the absolute "not another instance of the same one." Also fix the citations: the rule lives in templates/CONSTITUTION.md (lines 67, 97-98) and qa_ledger.py spec-check (lines 1739-1742, 1878), not in a judgment-day or sys-doc SKILL.md.

idea_drift.finding: Tenet 6 (profiles A-E) is the thesis's headline scaling mechanism but is pure marketing overreach: the words 'profile'/'perfil' appear only as vague prose asides ('risk profile C+/E'), with no A-E definition, no config field, and no code path. The one simplicity budget in dev-loop.config.json is global and static. The method claims rigor auto-scales to blast radius; the artifact makes the operator hand-tune one budget block and remember which prose aside applies.
idea_drift.fix: Either mechanize profiles (add defaults.profiles.{A..E} presets that select severity_gate + simplicity budgets + which optional gates run, and a --profile flag threaded through simplicity-check/pit-check/rebuild), or drop the 'profiles A-E' claim from the thesis and describe it honestly as 'per-project tunable budgets'.

idea_drift.finding: The CONSTITUTION is declared the apex of the truth hierarchy ('qué nunca es aceptable', enforced 'antes de tocar nada') and a breach is asserted to cap readiness <=65 and block convergence 'by construction' (SKILL.md:238). But NO code reads CONSTITUTION.md. The <=65 cap fires only on a BLOCKER/CRITICAL severity_count from a static-gate XML report (qa_ledger.py:888-890) or a manual escalate. A domain-invariant breach with no linter rule (e.g. 'numeración sin huecos', 'exactitud al centavo') is invisible to the engine — 'by construction' is false; it's 'by the agent remembering'.
idea_drift.fix: Soften the prose to 'the agent must escalate a breach; the engine caps readiness only once that breach is logged (escalate) or surfaced by a linter rule', OR add a constitution-check subcommand that at minimum verifies each invariant has a mapped enforcing mechanism and logs a BLOCKER when an inviolable checkbox lacks a gate.

idea_drift.finding: Maker != checker is stated in tenet 3 and printed as a CONSTITUTION invariant (INV gate-integrity, checkbox 'checker no-correlacionado con el maker'), but the kit itself admits inline 'eso es proceso, no código' (CONSTITUTION.md:98). It is a tenet asserted in prose and NOT mechanized: nothing verifies the reviewer differs from the author. This is honest but the checkbox-in-a-gated-doc framing implies enforcement that doesn't exist.
idea_drift.fix: Move the maker!=checker item out of the gate-integrity invariant checklist into an explicit 'process, not gated' note, so a reader doesn't assume golden-diff/gate-check enforce reviewer independence.

idea_drift.finding: Ceremony vs simplicity ethic (tenet 4 / Simplicidad invariant): the engine now carries 15+ subcommands including four overlapping diff/spec gates (simplicity-check, gate-check, spec-check, golden-diff, pit-check, rebuild), yet NONE of the optional gates feed the two decision functions — _converged (qa_ledger.py:632) and _repo_readiness (869) ignore simplicity/gate/pit/golden entirely. The operator must manually run each, read each verdict, and act. A methodology whose own CONSTITUTION forbids 'capas no solicitadas' ships a 2153-line engine where convergence is decided by a subset of it; the rest is ceremony the human must orchestrate by hand.
idea_drift.fix: Wire the fact-blocking gates (golden-diff, gate-check OVERBUILT/simplicity) into _converged so a repo cannot converge with an unapproved golden or a weakened gate, making the gates load-bearing rather than advisory ceremony the agent may skip.

idea_drift.finding: Tenet 7 'human owns the gate, always' is unmechanized where it matters most: the merge stop is prose-only (SKILL.md:210-214 'STOP') and cmd_escalate merely appends a ledger row (qa_ledger.py:695-703) with no consequence. Additionally the escalation readiness cap only applies while !converged (869 line 892), so once a repo converges a still-open escalation stops capping — a gap where the 'unresolved escalation <=75' guarantee silently lapses.
idea_drift.fix: Make the escalation cap independent of converged (cap while the escalation lacks a resolved/at timestamp), and add an explicit 'resolve-escalation' subcommand so the human closing the gate is a recorded event, not an implicit side effect of convergence.

idea_drift.finding: spec-check exists to make tenet-1 rigor deterministic, but its structural 'blockers' (missing out-of-scope section, no testable acceptance) are still only ADVISORY by default (qa_ledger.py:1826-1830,1859) — the same severity as an EARS-style nit. Per tenet 4 these two are FACTS (a section is present or absent, readable deterministically), so they should block, not advise. Filing a structural absence under the same advisory bucket as prose-guesses contradicts the kit's own 'facts block' rule.
idea_drift.fix: Split spec-check verdicts: the two structural blockers (absent out-of-scope, absent/empty acceptance) are facts and should exit 1 unconditionally; keep vague-term/EARS/stack-naming as advisory. This aligns spec-check with the fact/guess boundary the rest of the engine honors.

idea_drift.finding: The orchestrator SKILL.md — the doc a reader opens for 'run the dev loop' — never once mentions golden-diff, .approved, .received, or the PreToolUse hook. Yet tenet 5 ('the one artifact the agent cannot author') and INV-GOLDEN-01 are sold as the method's crown jewel, and the CONSTITUTION calls a clean golden-diff a 'hard close condition' for any touched module. A reader who follows the main skill flow end-to-end will build, QA-loop, and PR a migration WITHOUT ever capturing a golden or running golden-diff — silently skipping the tenet the marketing leans on hardest.
idea_drift.anchor: .claude/skills/dev-loop/SKILL.md Phase 1 (L62-76) and Phase 3 (L119-169) — no golden capture, no golden-diff, no hook, despite CONSTITUTION.md L70-80 making it a hard gate
idea_drift.fix: Add golden capture to Phase 1 (characterization) and golden-diff as an explicit convergence/close gate in Phase 3, plus wire the PreToolUse hook in the setup section. The mechanism exists in code and CONSTITUTION but is unreachable from the orchestrator the reader actually runs.

idea_drift.finding: The headline promise 'the ledger reads real artifacts; maker != checker' is only half-true. It holds for the static gate (ingest-gate parses XML, diffs finding-IDs) but NOT for the agent QA loop that runs every cycle: log-step accepts --reported/--gated-reported/--fixed as verbatim agent input and the convergence check trusts them. The same agent that made the change types its own findings count into the ledger. A reader expecting an independent checker for the primary loop is misled — 'maker != checker' is an unenforced process suggestion in the CONSTITUTION, not something the tool guarantees.
idea_drift.anchor: qa_ledger.py cmd_log_step L497-531 (stores agent counts verbatim) + _converged L632-655 (trusts agent gated_reported/files_changed/tests_passed); doc claim in SKILL.md L18 'never estimate counts from memory'
idea_drift.fix: Say plainly in SKILL.md that agent-tool counts are self-reported narration recorded for the retrospective, and that the non-correlated checker (maker != checker) is a human/process obligation the tool does not enforce — or add a mechanism (e.g. a second-agent re-review whose fingerprints the ledger diffs). Do not let 'the ledger reads real artifacts' imply the agent loop is independently verified.

idea_drift.finding: README advertises 'Cuatro skills (discovery, adr-refine, dev-loop, sys-doc)' but the kit ships SIX: characterize and reverse-discovery also exist — and those two are precisely where the golden-capture workflow and the hook wiring are documented (they're the only .md files besides CONSTITUTION/CHANGELOG that reference block-approved-writes). A reader trusting the README never learns the two skills that operationalize the golden tenet exist. Code does something valuable the doc hides.
idea_drift.anchor: README.md L4 'Cuatro skills' vs .claude/skills/ containing characterize/ and reverse-discovery/; hook referenced in characterize/SKILL.md and reverse-discovery/SKILL.md but not README
idea_drift.fix: Update README to list all six skills and place characterize/reverse-discovery in the end-to-end flow (they are the golden/legacy on-ramp). Fix the 'Qué hay adentro' tree (L11-21) too.

idea_drift.finding: Profiles A-E are cited as if defined (tenet 6 'rigor scales to blast radius (profiles A-E)'; SKILL.md Phase 5b 'risk profile C+/E'; CONSTITUTION 'alto blast-radius'), but no doc anywhere defines what A through E mean or how a reader selects one. The reader is told a graduated-rigor system exists and is referenced by name, then given no map. It reads as ceremony pointing at a spec that isn't shipped.
idea_drift.anchor: .claude/skills/dev-loop/SKILL.md L190 'risk profile C+/E'; no A-E table in README.md or any SKILL.md
idea_drift.fix: Add a short profiles A-E table (blast radius → which gates become mandatory: e.g. E requires golden + pit-check + non-correlated checker + rebuild). Either define the ladder or stop referencing named rungs.
